response.reason: This lens compares each NL contract's exact source/model identities for structural completeness, containment, owner-default-entry, guard/trigger-group consistency, and endpoint targets. HumanDriving/Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal are all declared, [*] -> HumanDriving satisfies root initial entry, HumanDriving->Autonomous on Power_On and HumanDriving->Autonomous on Front_Distance_10_2 both exist satisfying NL4-ENDPOINT (guard NL4-GUARD is unsupported since FCSTM has no guard field, kept W1), AutonomousActive->HumanDriving on Human_Steering_Cmd and Brake_Pressed exist and both events are reachable/consumed satisfying NL4.2-EVCOV partially. However AutonomousMode is NOT modeled as a composite/submachine state (Autonomous is a simple leaf state despite the <<submachine>> body tag), so NL2-DECL and the containment/cardinality contracts fail: there are no sub-states owned by Autonomous, and the actual sub-state chain Autonomous->AutonomousIdle->AutonomousActive is a flat sibling sequence, not contained within Autonomous. Also there is no distinct "auto final" sub-state reachable via `in (auto final)` as an alternative trigger into AutonomousActive->HumanDriving; the third alternative of the NL4.2 group (guard "in (auto final)") has no corresponding transition at all, and AutonomousFinal is a separate root-level leaf reached only via HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal (Power_Off), not connected to AutonomousMode's internal completion. This confirms the NL4.2-DERIVED termination-role obligation is violated: there is no "auto final" state within AutonomousMode's substructure at all, and the guard-only third alternative in the transition group has no realized transition, a distinct structural mismatch from the two event-based alternatives which do exist.

cardinality_bindings.reason: The behavior-consequence facts (reachability, state parentage) show that the closed FCSTM/inspection_equivalent_facts declares Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, and AutonomousFinal all with parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010 (the flat machine root), not parent=Autonomous. There is no owned composite state ref in closed_model_inventory.states[] that owns AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive as direct children; the FCSTM is flat despite the PlantUML <<submachine>> annotation on Autonomous. Because no exact owning composite ref exists, owner_source_id/owner_model_ref cannot be bound exactly, so this must remain ambiguous/unresolved rather than an exact direct_child_states reading with a false owner binding.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence properties: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, forbidden-scope entry, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. The closed FCSTM (case 0010) is a flat model with states HumanDriving, Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, AutonomousFinal, all reachable from root. AutonomousFinal is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostic, verify_facts deadlock check status=refuted). The termination contract NL5-TERMINATION-1 requires the system to terminate at "final state" on power off; the actual carrier AutonomousFinal has no outgoing transition (it is a true sink, not a UML final pseudostate [*]), which is consistent with stable termination in one reading, but the model never declares an actual PlantUML/FCSTM final-state marker (no [*] target), so termination is only nominal (a named sink state) rather than a formally marked completion. I flag this as a predicate-null W1 concern under the termination contract since the frozen registry has no term for "is this named sink truly a UML final state." For NL4.2-EVCOV-1 (event consumer coverage for human steering cmd / brake pressed inside AutonomousMode), the flat model's AutonomousActive state (mapped to the composite's active substate) is the exact and only reachable consumer for Human_Steering_Cmd (transition:line:17) and Brake_Pressed (transition:line:18); both are reachable from initial per inspection_equivalent_facts. This coverage is satisfied, so no candidate is needed for that contract on this behavioral basis alone. However AutonomousMode is realized as a set of flat leaf states (Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive) rather than one true composite with substates, which is already flagged by the sibling structural lens under containment/cardinality; the behavior-consequence facts here (reachability, consumer reachability) are otherwise satisfied for the observed structure. I derive one candidate for the true dead-end: AutonomousFinal has no outgoing transition and no formal completion marker, which under a strict systems-level termination reading is a possible violation of stable termination since the model never actually models completion (no [*] end pseudostate), keeping the model perpetually stuck rather than terminating in a UML sense. This is preserved as predicate-null (no V1/S2 predicate captures "is this leaf a true UML final state") under the existing termination contract rather than inventing a new one, since termination is exactly the property already declared by NL-CONTRACT-REF-009. For the cardinality contract on AutonomousMode's direct-child sub-states, I return an ambiguous/unbound row because the closed FCSTM realizes AutonomousMode's intended substructure as flat sibling leaf states (Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive) rather than one exact composite state that owns them as declared children in closed_model_inventory.states[].ref; there is no unique owned composite state ref that owns AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive as its direct children, so owner_source_id/owner_model_ref cannot be bound exactly from this behavioral facts set.
